definition: The USA PATRIOT Act (commonly referred to as the Patriot Act) is a shorthand name for The Uniting and Strengthening America by Providing Appropriate Tools Required to Intercept and Obstruct Terrorism Act. The Act was passed on October 26, 2001, shortly after the terrorist attacks of September 11th. The legislation was intended to bolster national security and broader law enforcement and intelligence authorities, as well as to more effectively address domestic and international terrorism. Among other things, the Act:  Expanded federal resources and authorities for counterterrorism and security procedures, including increasing funding for law enforcement agencies.  Expanded and modified federal electronic surveillance capabilities and intelligence-gathering authorities.  Reduced legal and institutional barriers to investigating suspected acts of terrorism, including easing interagency communication and encouraging information sharing. unseasoned issuer / USA PATRIOT Act Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026  Increased the penalties for acts of terrorism and expanded the list of activities considered to be acts of terrorism. Some of the USA PATRIOT Act surveillance authorities were scheduled to expire in 2015. The USA FREEDOM Act, (shorthand for Uniting and Strengthening America by Fulfilling Rights and Ensuring Effective Discipline Over Monitoring Act of 2015), enacted on June 2, 2015, extended, modified, or allowed the expiration of various USA PATRIOT Act authorities; including the end of the statutory basis for the National Security Administration’s (NSA’s) bulk collection of domestic telephone metadata under Section 215.
